questions.question: From the alternatives given below, choose the correct meaning of the idiom 'more power to your elbow'.

options.text: To interact or mingle with a person or group
May you find success in your activity or pursuit
To force one's way through (a crowd or crowded place) by or as by pushing other people with one's elbows

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **May you find success in your activity or pursuit**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **'more power to your elbow'** is an expression of **encouragement** used to wish someone **success** or **good luck** in an activity they are undertaking. (किसी के कार्य में सफलता की कामना करना या प्रोत्साहन देना)
 
 
• **Example: **I heard you are starting your own consultancy; **more power to your elbow**!
 
 
 
• **'May you find success in your activity or pursuit'** directly defines the sentiment of wishing someone **achievement** and **prosperity** in their specific efforts or goals. (अपनी गतिविधि या प्रयास में सफलता प्राप्त करना)
 
 
• **Example: **As you prepare for your final examinations, **may you find success in your pursuit**.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct meaning of the idiom is to wish someone well in their endeavors.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **May you find success in your activity or pursuit**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

__
 
• **To drink alcohol, perhaps excessively** (शराब पीना, शायद अत्यधिक): This phrase is often associated with the idiom **'to bend one's elbow'**.
 
 
• **Example:** He has been **bending his elbow** at the tavern every night this week.
 
 
 
• **To interact or mingle with a person or group** (किसी व्यक्ति या समूह के साथ मेलजोल करना): This meaning is usually expressed by the idiom **'to rub elbows'**.
 
 
• **Example: **The conference provided a great opportunity to **rub elbows** with top industry professionals.
 
 
 
• **To force one's way through (a crowd or crowded place)** (भीड़ के माध्यम से कोहनी मारते हुए या धकेलते हुए रास्ता बनाना): This describes the literal or figurative act of **'elbowing one's way'** through a group.
 
 
• **Example:** We had to **elbow our way through** the heavy crowd to reach the subway entrance.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Will they have finalised the plans by the end of this week?

options.text: The plans will be finalised by them by the end of this week.
Will the plans be finalised by them by the end of this week?
They will have finalised the plans by the end of this week?
Will the plans have been finalised by them by the end of this week?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will the plans have been finalised by them by the end of this week?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an **Interrogative Sentence** in the **Future Perfect Tense**. The active structure is: **Will + Subject + have + V3 (Past Participle) + Object + ?**.
 
• To convert a **Future Perfect** interrogative sentence into **Passive Voice**, the following structure is applied: **Will + New Subject (Original Object) + have been + V3 (Past Participle) + by + New Object (Original Subject) + ?**.
 
• In this sentence, the subject is **they**, the verb is **finalised**, and the object is **the plans**. Following the rule, the object **the plans** becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The auxiliary verb **have been** must be used immediately after the new subject in the passive form to maintain the **Perfect Tense** aspect.
 
• The pronoun **they** is the subject in the active voice and changes to its objective case **them** when it becomes the agent in the passive voice.
 
• The phrase **by the end of this week** is an adverbial of time and remains at the end of the sentence to maintain the original meaning.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tense Transitions in Passive Voice:**
 
 
• **Future Indefinite:** Changes from **will + V1** to **will be + V3**. Options using **will be finalised** are incorrect because the original sentence is in the perfect tense.
 
• **Future Perfect:** Changes from **will have + V3** to **will have been + V3**. This transition is essential to show that the action will have been completed.
 
• **Assertive vs. Interrogative:** An interrogative active sentence must remain interrogative in its passive form. Options that change the sentence into a statement (Assertive) are grammatically incorrect for this transformation.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Agent:** The use of **by them** indicates the **doer** of the action. In passive voice, the emphasis shifts from the doer (**they**) to the receiver of the action (**the plans**).
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Does the guard wave the flags at every passing train?

options.text: Is the flags waved by the guard at every passing train?
Did the flags waved by the guard at every passing train?
Are the flags waved by the guard at every passing train?
Do the flags waved by the guard at every passing train?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Are the flags waved by the guard at every passing train?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is an interrogative sentence in the **Active Voice**, specifically in the **Simple Present Tense**, identified by the auxiliary verb **Does**.
 
• In **Active Voice**, the structure for a **Simple Present** question is: **Do/Does + Subject + Base Verb (V1) + Object?**. Here, **the guard** is the subject and **the flags** is the object.
 
• To convert an interrogative sentence into **Passive Voice**, the object of the active sentence (**the flags**) becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The passive structure for **Simple Present** interrogatives is: **Is/Am/Are + New Subject + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent?**.
 
• Since the new subject **the flags** is **plural**, the plural auxiliary verb **Are** must be used at the beginning of the sentence to maintain **Subject-Verb Agreement**.
 
• The primary verb **wave** is converted into its **Past Participle** form, which is **waved**.
 
• The original subject **the guard** is introduced as the agent following the preposition **by**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement**:
 
 
• In English grammar, the verb must match the number of the subject. Using **Is** with a plural noun like **the flags** is a grammatical error.
 
 
 
• **Tense Consistency**:
 
 
• The use of **Did** is characteristic of the **Simple Past Tense**. Converting a present tense active sentence into a past tense passive sentence changes the original meaning and is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Passive Voice Components**:
 
 
• A standard passive construction always requires a form of the verb **to be** (is, am, are, was, were) combined with the **Past Participle (V3)**. Options starting with **Do** or **Did** while using **waved** do not follow the standard structural requirements of passive voice.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
A secret message was delivered by the courier yesterday.

options.text: The courier delivers a secret message yesterday.
The courier was delivering a secret message yesterday.
The courier delivered a secret message yesterday.
The courier had delivered a secret message yesterday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The courier delivered a secret message yesterday.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence 'A secret message was delivered by the courier yesterday' is in the **Passive Voice**. This is identified by the auxiliary verb **was** followed by the past participle **delivered** and the preposition **by**. Hence, the sentence structure follows the **Simple Past Passive** format: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject.

• To convert a sentence from passive to active voice, the **Object** of the passive sentence (the courier) must become the **Subject** of the active sentence. Hence, 'The courier' initiates the action.

• The original subject (a secret message) becomes the **direct object** in the active voice construction. Hence, it receives the action of the verb.

• The tense of the sentence is **Simple Past**. In the active voice, the verb must be in its **V2 (Simple Past)** form without any auxiliary verbs like 'was' or 'were'. The V2 form of 'deliver' is **delivered**. Hence, the verb phrase changes from 'was delivered' to 'delivered'.

• The **Adverb of Time** 'yesterday' remains unchanged and typically stays at the end of the sentence to maintain the original meaning and chronological context. Hence, the final active construction is 'The courier delivered a secret message yesterday.'

 **Additional Information__**

• Rules for **Voice Conversion** in different tenses:

• **Simple Present Tense**:

• Active: Subject + V1(s/es) + Object.

• Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject.

• **Past Continuous Tense**:

• Active: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

• Passive: Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject.

• **Past Perfect Tense**:

• Active: Subject + had + V3 + Object.

• Passive: Object + had + been + V3 + by + Subject.

• Analysis of incorrect options:

• **Delivers**: This represents the **Simple Present Tense**, which contradicts the past time marker 'yesterday'.

• **Was delivering**: This represents the **Past Continuous Tense**, indicating an ongoing action in the past rather than a completed one.

• **Had delivered**: This represents the **Past Perfect Tense**, used to describe an action completed before another point in the past, which is not required here.

</ul

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

It was very odd _______ the man to give advice to his master.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**of**'. **__Key Points__** __ 
• The preposition **'of'** is used in the construction **'It + be + adjective + of + person + to-infinitive'**. 
• This pattern is used to evaluate a person's character or behavior in a specific situation. Adjectives commonly used in this structure include **kind, nice, silly, brave, polite,** and **odd**. 
• In the given sentence, the word **'odd'** is used to describe the nature of the man's behavior (giving advice to his master), necessitating the use of **'of'**. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. **Complete Sentence:** *'It was very **odd of**__ the man to give advice to his master.'* **__Additional Information__** 
• **Option 2: 'about'** is generally used to indicate the subject matter or topic and does not fit this idiomatic structure. 
• **Option 3: 'in'** is used for location or containers and is grammatically incorrect here. 
• **Option 4: 'for'** is used in a similar structure (**It + be + adjective + for + person + to-infinitive**), but primarily when the adjective describes the **action** itself (e.g., hard, easy, important, necessary) rather than the **person's character**. </ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."

The activist insisted that __the people should call spade__ a spade and confront corruption directly.

options.text: the people need to call spades
the people must call a spade a spade
the people have to call spades a spade

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the people must call a spade a spade**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The phrase **call a spade a spade** is a standard **English idiom** that means to speak **plainly and bluntly** about something as it is, without using **euphemisms** or beating around the bush.

• Grammatically, **idioms** are fixed expressions. The original sentence used **call spade a spade**, which is incorrect because it lacks the **indefinite article 'a'** before the first **spade**. Proper idiomatic usage requires the structure **call a spade a spade**.

• The verb **insisted** in the main clause denotes a **strong demand** or a firm stance. The **modal verb 'must'** is more appropriate than **'should'** in this context as it emphasizes **necessity and obligation**, aligning with the activist's forceful tone.

• By replacing the phrase with **the people must call a spade a spade**, the sentence achieves both **idiomatic accuracy** and **contextual emphasis**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Idiomatic Integrity**:

• The phrase has its roots in **Ancient Greek** and was introduced into **English** via **Erasmus** in the **16th century**. It is essential to maintain the **singular form** and include the **articles** to preserve its meaning.

• Option 1 (**call spades**) and Option 3 (**call spades a spade**) are incorrect because they change the **plurality** of the noun, which violates the fixed nature of the idiom.

• **Modal Verbs**:

• **Must**: Expresses **subjective obligation** or a requirement imposed by the speaker. In this case, the **activist** imposes this requirement on the people.

• **Should**: Generally expresses **advice or suggestion**, which is weaker than what the verb **insisted** implies.

</ul

questions.question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. One day at the hotel, passing through the bar, he saw that old Brevald, as ever in his shabby blue overalls, was standing there. 

A. His manner was not agreeable. 

B. They chatted for a few minutes of local affairs, and Lawson was uneasily conscious that the Norwegian was scrutinizing him with sly blue eyes. 

C. It was sycophantic, and yet behind the cringing air of an old man who had been worsted in his struggle with fate was a shadow of old truculence. 

D. Because he was Ethel's father, he had a desire to speak to him, so he went in, nodded and, ordering his own drink, casually turned and invited the old man to have one with him. 

S2. Lawson remembered that he had once been captain of a schooner engaged in the slave trade, a blackbirder they call it in the Pacific, and he had a large hernia in the chest which was the result of a wound received in a scrap with Solomon Islanders.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes an interaction between a character named **Lawson** and an old man named **Brevald** at a hotel bar. 
• **Sentence D follows S1** as it provides the immediate reaction to seeing **Brevald** at the bar. Since Brevald is **Ethel's father**, Lawson decides to enter the bar and invite the old man for a drink: 
• 'Because he was Ethel's father, he had a desire to speak to him, so he went in, nodded and, ordering his own drink, casually turned and invited the old man to have one with him.' 
• **Sentence B follows D** because it describes the conversation and interaction that took place after the drink was ordered. It mentions they **chatted about local affairs** while Lawson felt the **Norwegian** (Brevald) was **scrutinizing** him: 
• 'They chatted for a few min of local affairs, and Lawson was uneasily conscious that the Norwegian was scrutinizing him with sly blue eyes.' 
• **Sentence A follows B** as it moves from the specific action of scrutiny to a general observation about Brevald's **manner** or behavior during this chat: 
• 'His manner was not agreeable.' 
• **Sentence C follows A** because it elaborates on the **manner** mentioned in the previous sentence, describing it as **sycophantic** yet hiding a shadow of **truculence** (aggressiveness): 
• 'It was sycophantic, and yet behind the cringing air of an old man who had been worsted in his struggle with fate was a shadow of old truculence.' 
• Finally, **S2** concludes the paragraph by providing the historical context for that truculence, revealing Brevald's past as a **blackbirder** (slave trader) and his physical scars from **Solomon Islanders**. 
• The correct sequence is **DBAC**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'One day at the hotel, passing through the bar, he saw that old Brevald, as ever in his shabby blue overalls, was standing there. Because he was Ethel's father, he had a desire to speak to him, so he went in, nodded and, ordering his own drink, casually turned and invited the old man to have one with him. They chatted for a few min of local affairs, and Lawson was uneasily conscious that the Norwegian was scrutinizing him with sly blue eyes. His manner was not agreeable. It was sycophantic, and yet behind the cringing air of an old man who had been worsted in his struggle with fate was a shadow of old truculence. Lawson remembered that he had once been captain of a schooner engaged in the slave trade, a blackbirder they call it in the Pacific, and he had a large hernia in the chest which was the result of a wound received in a scrap with Solomon Islanders.'</div

A. The Garnets had two daughters besides, one of sixteen and the other of twelve, but however unreasonable it seemed, for a father is generally supposed to like his daughters best, and though he did all he could not to show his preference, there was no doubt that the greater share of Henry Garnet's affection was given to his son. 

B. His name was Nicholas and of course he was called Nicky. 

C. He was kind, in a chaffing, casual way, to his daughters, and gave them handsome presents on their birthdays and at Christmas; but he doted on Nicky. 

D. He was eighteen.

S2. Nothing was too good for him.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph focuses on the relationship between a father, **Henry Garnet**, and his children, specifically highlighting his deep affection for his **only son**. 
• **Sentence S1 is fixed** and introduces the subject: **the boy** who is the **only son**. 
• **Sentence B follows S1** as it provides the basic identification of the boy mentioned: 
• 'His name was **Nicholas** and of course he was called **Nicky**.' 
• **Sentence D is the second sentence** in the sequence as it continues the description of the son by mentioning his age: 
• 'He was **eighteen**.' 
• **Sentence A is the third sentence** as it introduces other family members, the **two daughters**, and establishes the contrast in the father’s feelings: 
• 'The **Garnets** had **two daughters** besides... but there was no doubt that the greater share of **Henry Garnet's affection** was given to his **son**.' 
• **Sentence C is the fourth sentence** as it elaborates on how he treated the daughters versus his son, reinforcing the preference mentioned in A: 
• 'He was kind... to his **daughters**... but he **doted on Nicky**.' 
• **Sentence S2 is fixed** and perfectly concludes the thought by showing the extent of his devotion: '**Nothing was too good for him**.' 
• The correct sequence is **BDAC**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'The boy of whom he spoke was his **only son**. His name was **Nicholas** and of course he was called **Nicky**. He was **eighteen**. The **Garnets** had **two daughters** besides, one of sixteen and the other of twelve, but however unreasonable it seemed, for a father is generally supposed to like his daughters best, and though he did all he could not to show his preference, there was no doubt that the greater share of **Henry Garnet's affection** was given to his **son**. He was kind, in a chaffing, casual way, to his **daughters**, and gave them handsome presents on their birthdays and at Christmas; but he **doted on Nicky**. **Nothing was too good for him**.'

• The phrase **for all intents and purposes** is a fixed **idiomatic expression** in the English language that means **in every practical sense**, **virtually**, or **essentially**.

• It is used to describe a situation where, although some **technicalities** or **minor details** might suggest otherwise, the overall **outcome** or **status** is effectively settled. In the given sentence, the project is considered **finished** for any **practical application**, despite the mention of **final touches**.

• Grammatically, the phrase requires the **plural noun intents**, which refers to **intentions** or **aims**. This acts as a **complement** to the word **purposes**.

• The original sentence used **intends**, which is the **third-person singular verb** form of **intend**. Using a **verb** in this position is **grammatically incorrect** as the structure of the **prepositional phrase** requires **coordinated nouns**.

• The **syntactic structure** of the idiom involves two **nouns** joined by the **conjunction and**, creating a **legalistic redundancy** typical of **Early Modern English**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Linguistic Errors and Eggcorns**:

• **For all intensive purposes**: This is a classic example of an **eggcorn**, a phonetic **misinterpretation** of a phrase that sounds similar to the original but changes its meaning. **Intensive** is an **adjective** meaning **concentrated** or **thorough**, which does not logically fit the **adverbial** usage of the idiom.

• **For all intense and purposes**: This is a **malapropism** where the **adjective intense** (meaning extreme or acute) is substituted for the **noun intents**. It is **semantically nonsensical** in this context.

• **Historical Origins**:

• The expression dates back to **16th-century English law**. It was originally found in the **Act of Supremacy (1534)** in the form **to all intents, constructions and purposes**. Over centuries, the phrase was shortened and the **preposition for** became common in **American English**, while **to** remains frequent in **British English**.

</ul

questions.question:
The Himalayas are considered among the most ecologically fragile regions because various factors make the region exceptionally difficult.

Which of the following best sums up these difficulties?

options.text: Geological instability, human pressures, and climate change
Soil fertility, agricultural expansion, and urbanization
High rainfall, dense forests, and biodiversity richness
Tourism growth, cultural diversity, and economic development

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the passage, the **Himalayas** are described as a highly fragile region due to specific environmental and human-induced factors.
 
• The text explicitly identifies **geological instability**, increasing **anthropogenic pressures** (human-related pressures), and the impacts of **climate change** as the primary difficulties.
 
• These factors collectively endanger the unique **mountain biodiversity** and the livelihood of millions of people living **downstream**.
 
• Option 1 directly mirrors the challenges mentioned in the first sentence of the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** While agricultural expansion and urbanization are forms of human pressure, **soil fertility** is generally a positive trait and not listed as a reason for ecological fragility in this text.
 
• **Option 3:** High rainfall and dense forests contribute to the region's ecology, but they are not cited as the **difficulties** or threats making the region fragile.
 
• **Option 4:** Although tourism and economic development can contribute to human pressure, the passage focuses on the broader categories of **geological instability** and **climate change** as the defining difficulties.
</ul

questions.question: Why does the passage indicate that isolated conservation efforts are not enough?

options.text: They disregard the function of indigenous species in ecosystems
They hinder species' ability to migrate and adjust to warming temperatures.
They eliminate the necessity for government engagement in conservation
They decrease the value of biodiversity in global ecosystems

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage highlights that the **Himalayas** are an ecologically fragile region facing **geological instability** and the impacts of **climate change**.
 
• It explicitly states that protecting **isolated locations** is not enough to conserve **indigenous species**.
 
• For species to survive **rising temperatures**, they need to be able to **migrate and adjust**, which is only possible if protected areas are connected at the **landscape level**.
 
• Isolated conservation efforts essentially act as barriers that **hinder this migration**, preventing species from moving to more suitable habitats as the climate warms.

Therefore, the correct answer is **They hinder species' ability to migrate and adjust to warming temperatures.**

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** The passage does not claim that isolation causes a disregard for the **function** of species, but rather it restricts their **movement**.
 
• **Option 3:** The passage emphasizes that **government engagement** and coordinated action are **essential**, not eliminated by isolated efforts.
 
• **Option 4:** The **value of biodiversity** remains high; the issue is the **resilience** and survival of that biodiversity in the face of warming, which is compromised by lack of connectivity.
</ul

questions.question: Which approach does the passage recommend for long-term biodiversity protection in the Himalayas?

options.text: Limiting conservation efforts to local community initiatives
Creating landscape-level linkages between protected areas
Reducing government participation in conservation programs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explicitly states that **protecting isolated locations** is insufficient for the long-term conservation of **indigenous species**.
 
• It highlights that species require the ability to **migrate and adjust** to rising temperatures, which is facilitated when **protected areas are connected**.
 
• The recommended strategy for long-term protection is the creation of **landscape-level linkages** between these areas to ensure ecological continuity.
 
• This approach aims to increase the **resilience** of the **Himalayan biodiversity** against the impacts of **climate change** and human pressures.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Creating landscape-level linkages between protected areas**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The passage recommends **creating landscape-level linkages between protected areas** as the approach for long-term biodiversity protection in the Himalayas."*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** The passage calls for **coordinated action** from various groups, not just limiting efforts to **local community initiatives**.
 
• **Option 2:** Establishing **isolated reserves** is the exact approach the passage identifies as **inadequate** for modern conservation needs.
 
• **Option 4:** The text mentions that **government participation** is **essential**, so reducing it would be counterproductive to the conservation strategy.
</ul

questions.question: What steps should be taken, according to the passage, to ensure the Himalayas' future?

options.text: Relying solely on technology to preserve biodiversity
Outright forbidding human activity in mountainous areas
Cutting back on conservation initiatives to save money
Quick, well-coordinated actions involving several stakeholders

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage emphasizes that the **Himalayas** are a highly fragile region facing severe threats from **geological instability**, **anthropogenic pressures**, and **climate change**.
 
• To address these challenges, the text calls for an **urgent, comprehensive conservation strategy** rather than isolated efforts.
 
• It specifically mentions that **immediate, coordinated action** from various groups, including **governments**, **communities**, and other **stakeholders**, is essential to secure the region's future.
 
• Therefore, the steps to be taken involve **quick, well-coordinated actions involving several stakeholders**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because the passage does not suggest that **technology** is the sole solution for preserving biodiversity.
 
• **Option 2** is incorrect as the passage advocates for **coordinated action** and management rather than a total **outright ban** on all human activity.
 
• **Option 3** is incorrect because the passage argues for an **urgent and comprehensive strategy**, which implies increasing rather than **cutting back** on conservation initiatives.
</ul
